This page sets out the exercise, task by task, with the tool in which each task is done. The [background page](../../background.qmd) presents the original study, the robustness study of SCORE (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026) and the five reanalyses. Every task of the session is done in its deck, whose slides run R inside your browser with the data already in place, and the [browser lab](../../lab.qmd) is the fallback if the deck will not load.

## The tasks {#the-tasks}

The session takes three of the five tasks of the exercise at the keyboard, all three in the deck, and keeps the estimand statement of Task 2 as an answer that you write in the chat. The causal graph of Task 2 and the preregistration of Task 5 are not part of the session.

### Task 1 – Get yourself running {#task-1-get-yourself-running}

Open the deck, wait until the cell on its second slide shows a "Run Code" button, run it, and check that it reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years.

### The estimand statement {#the-estimand-statement}

On the slides of the first half, write the estimand of the claim in one sentence.

### Task 3 – Reproduce a recorded result {#task-3-reproduce-a-recorded-result}

Choose one of the three analysts whose results rest on aggregate data, C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, and refit the analysis until the value on record comes back to the third decimal. Each of the three has a slide of its own in the deck, whose cells you run in order, and each cell with gaps to fill has a hint and a full solution under it.

### Task 4 – Work the menu {#task-4-work-the-menu}

This task is **exploratory**. On the three slides of the hands-on in the second half, call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Every argument of `try_spec()` defaults to the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR on which the [specification menu](../../menu.qmd) and the curve are built. Then submit the one that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`, and your dot is drawn on the live [class chart](../../class-results.qmd) as an exploratory result.

In the cell of the placement slide, rerun the specification that you submitted with `try_spec()` and read off your placement among the 864 specifications of the curve.
